import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.feature_selection import mutual_info_classif
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

MAX_DRIVERS = 4

def design(feats):
    # Filter out near-duplicates based on correlation
    ids = list(feats.ids)
    types = list(feats.types)
    
    # Remove near-duplicates (|r| >= 0.6)
    keep = []
    seen = set()
    for i, id1 in enumerate(ids):
        if id1 in seen:
            continue
        keep.append(i)
        # Check correlations with later features
        for j in range(i+1, len(ids)):
            id2 = ids[j]
            if id2 in seen:
                continue
            col1 = feats.column(id1)
            col2 = feats.column(id2)
            corr = np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, col1], feats.x[:, col2])[0,1]
            if abs(corr) >= 0.6:
                seen.add(id2)
    
    filtered_ids = [ids[i] for i in keep]
    filtered_types = [types[i] for i in keep]
    
    # Compute effect sizes (mean difference in outcome groups)
    effects = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(filtered_ids):
        col = feats.column(fid)
        y = feats.y
        mean1 = np.mean(feats.x[y==1, col])
        mean0 = np.mean(feats.x[y==0, col])
        effect = mean1 - mean0
        effects.append((abs(effect), i, fid))
    
    # Sort by effect size
    effects.sort(reverse=True)
    
    # Select top drivers (at most MAX_DRIVERS)
    drivers = [fid for _, _, fid in effects[:MAX_DRIVERS]]
    
    # For logistic regression, include all features with strong effects
    columns = []
    products = []
    loadings = {}
    
    # Include all features with |effect| > 0.1
    for _, i, fid in effects:
        if abs(effects[i][0]) > 0.1:
            columns.append(fid)
            
    # Add interaction terms between top features
    top_features = [fid for _, _, fid in effects[:3]]
    for i in range(len(top_features)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(top_features)):
            products.append((top_features[i], top_features[j]))
    
    # Weighted score using top features
    for i, (_, _, fid) in enumerate(effects[:3]):
        loadings[fid] = 1.0 / (i + 1)
    
    return Design(
        drivers=tuple(drivers),
        columns=tuple(columns),
        products=tuple(products),
        loadings=loadings
    )
